Study on Bench2Drive and NAVSIM: a high-resolution BEV lets the planner latch onto spurious landmarks, masking 20 % of cells plus patchifying helps (driving score 66.9 to 82.6), disentangled path plus speed outputs beat entangled trajectories, and commands are weak conditioning. Warns against feeding a dense raster to our consumer, whose graph tokens are already compressed; no route-format or map-quality ablation. Blockers: CARLA-based evidence, no repository. Context: supports route as lane attribute, no action.

Lane waypoints become graph-transformer vertices joined to their 20 nearest neighbours in feature space (not map connectivity) and feed a differentiable integrated prediction and planning optimiser; planning error at 3 s 1.710 m against 1.726 m for DIPP on Waymo. Nothing for our graph: Waymo ground-truth map and agent-centric prediction; the only point of interest is an example of a feature-space neighbour graph. Not relevant: out of scope.

Recipe study on MapTR / HIMap with camera + LiDAR: augmentation, cross-modal fusion and whole-feature modality dropout; augmentation gave the largest gain (+4.5 mAP on MapTR, against +3.3 fusion and +1.6 dropout) and the parts help only together. It backs our failure-frame training and suggests emulating dropout with foundation features cached per failure condition. Blockers: needs separable modality maps, end-to-end training with the host's Hungarian loss, no code. Use as the recipe reference for A8; deep extraction queued.
extract: skip: no repository in the note; search only when robustness work starts

text: Near-identity module between a frozen fused BEV map and an unchanged head: global shift normalisation, a LiDAR-density reliability map, a gated expert residual and a three-stage curriculum with an independent p = 0.30 corruption mix; largest gains for low light, rain lens, beam loss and fog, small for 6-camera dropout (+1.2 mAP). Closest published match to our interface (frozen features in, same-shaped features out), but its reliability map is trained on LiDAR point counts only (target 1 for camera faults), identity is only approximate, there are no seeds, no plain fine-tune control and no code. Use: re-implement Block 1 and the gated residual on cached rasters with an exact-identity start and a paired-feature damage target.

TrustGate pools the LiDAR BEV into one scalar trust that blends a LiDAR-guided and a vision-only expert, plus a learned element-wise FailSafe gate; three-phase training keeps the backbone frozen under modality dropout. Same setting as ours (frozen backbone, failure training), and the scalar gate costs about 0.05 ms, but results are LiDAR-drop detection only. Blocker: needs a sensor-separable BEV pair; ours would blend repaired and raw features; no code. Use: port the gate and the three-phase recipe as our A8 trust gate.
extract: skip: no repository in the note; search only when robustness work starts

text: Classic calibration paper: temperature scaling of the logits and expected calibration error (ECE) as the measure. We already use both in E109 for the keep and route probabilities. It serves A8 and A4: calibration of per-vertex and per-fork probabilities is an open item that no paper measures. No blocker (register entry is abstract-level only); use: keep ECE plus temperature scaling as the baseline for every new probability.

Benchmarks how calibration and predictive uncertainty degrade when the data shift away from training: a protocol, not a method. Our failure series (night, blur, cameras off, radar off) is such a shift, and E109 already checks the calibration of keep and route probabilities under failure. Nothing to port; the register entry is abstract-level only. Use: keep reporting ECE per failure condition, not only on clean frames.

Eight corruptions at three severities (Bright, Dark, Fog, Snow, Motion Blur, Color Quant, Camera Crash, Frame Lost) on nuScenes val, scored by the ratio RR = corrupted / clean; CVT map segmentation falls from 0.348 IoU to 0.200 under Camera Crash and Dark. It is the published yardstick for our own failure series (night, blur, cameras off), whose conditions we can reproduce and report as RR per severity. Blockers: camera-only models, first paper seen by listing only. Use as test-bed definition and metric.

Dense BEV queries cross-attend to camera and LiDAR BEV features, a missing modality is simply left out, and switched-modality training feeds camera-only, LiDAR-only or both at one third each. One of the few papers with BEV map segmentation under sensor loss (mIoU with camera missing 53.7 against 4.1 for zero-filled BEVFusion), showing that zero-filling a lost input is a poor baseline; our failure series already has cameras-off and radar-off modes. Blocker: needs separable modality BEV maps, conflicts with our pre-fused frozen raster. Context only.

Ten corruptions for LiDAR-camera detection, among them spatial misalignment (extrinsic rotation and translation offsets), temporal misalignment and randomly missing camera frames, scored by resistance ability RA = corrupted / clean NDS (mRA: CMT 0.865, BEVFusion 0.830). Gives a ready recipe to synthesise extrinsic and temporal misalignment for our failure series and to report RA-style ratios next to RoboBEV's RR. Blockers: detection only, LiDAR-camera, no map outputs; a frozen foundation cannot repair wrong extrinsics. Use as test-bed recipe, effort S.

Online map heads output a Laplace location and scale per vertex (Laplace NLL instead of L1) and trajectory predictors (HiVT, DenseTNT) take mu, b and class probabilities; miss rate improves up to 15 % (HiVT + MapTR 0.0981 -> 0.0834). Touches our vertex output and planner consumer (register lists K87 under E109, E115): a per-vertex log-scale would add the positional confidence we lack (we carry validity only) and a failure signal. Blockers: some DenseTNT cells get worse, calibration not measured, heavy stack. Use: add a Laplace scale to vertices.

Challenge report (140 teams, five tracks; top entries used heavy augmentation, fusion and self-supervised error correction) and the Samsung-RAL map-segmentation entry: BEVerse with Swin backbones, a temporal module and image augmentations. Its lever ranking (backbone Tiny to Base +7.8 mIoU, temporal +2.4, then augmentation) fits our finding that head-side remedies on a frozen foundation restore only part of the loss, and supports a temporal hold. Blockers: camera-only, trainable backbone, tables mix phases 1 and 2. Context only.

Two plug-ins for camera mappers: G-PVR rebuilds a missing view's features from the other views, and D-BEVC pulls the BEV feature of the incomplete input toward that of the complete input with an MSE loss (missing-front mAP on MapTR 31.3 -> 42.4). D-BEVC transfers: a clean-teacher MSE on our cached features can train a repair module at no inference cost, which our failure fine-tuning (task loss only) has not tried. Blockers: G-PVR needs image features; host loss uses Hungarian matching. Use D-BEVC only, effort S.

When a modality drops, a memory of the last 6 frames' features is attended by a learnable BEV query to predict the missing feature, and an MLP adds a per-cell variance that down-weights the compensated feature; hosts stay frozen. It is the learned version of our training-free spatial hold (copy the warped previous input): predict the current feature from warped past features, with a variance. Blockers: needs a per-frame 'input missing' signal (our heat monitor could give it), code only announced, detection only. Use: re-implement as the learned hold.

Eight camera perturbations (blurs, motion blurs, lens attack) and three radar perturbations (depth error, ghost targets, disappearance) on RADIANT and CRN detection; vertical motion blur kernel 20 drops CRN mAP from 0.473 to 0.4066, while radar depth error of 200 % barely changes RADIANT. Camera damage far exceeds radar damage, which supports putting blur and night first in our failure mix; CRN was our early foundation. Blockers: detection only; reliability and failover are suggested but not evaluated. Context only.

Background on three test-time adaptation primitives: AdaBN swaps BN statistics for target statistics, TENT also minimises prediction entropy over BN scale and shift, SAR drops high-gradient samples and takes a sharpness-aware step for mixed shifts and small batches. We already tried adaptive BN (+0.04); RB22 shows plain AdaBN / TENT can collapse at batch 1, so SAR-style filtered entropy on the dense lane heat map is the untested next step. Blocker: abstract-level read, no BEV or lane results. Context only.

CoTTA keeps a weight-averaged teacher with augmentation-averaged predictions and stochastic weight restore; RoTTA adds a category-balanced memory bank and time-aware reweighting for correlated streams such as driving; DAT updates only two small parameter groups for driving segmentation. Relates to test-time adaptation of our lane head (A8): only adaptive BN was tried, and RoTTA's bank is the closest to a streaming drive. Blockers: none evaluated on BEV or lane outputs, CoTTA multiplies forward passes, abstract-level read. Watch; revisit if adaptive BN proves fragile.

Both modalities are mapped to BEV with the same deformable-attention scheme and fused by channel-normalised weights over the available modalities only (missing ones skipped, not zero-filled), trained with modality dropout 0.5; camera-only mAP 35.0 against 22.6 for BEVFusion. Explains the safe fusion operator for missing sensors, but our fusion sits inside the frozen GaussianCaR, so only a post-hoc analogue is possible. Blockers: LiDAR-camera detection, needs separable BEV maps, map segmentation left as future work. Context only.

Random camera views are masked at feature level in training and a masked-view reconstruction module (learned mask tokens, 3D position embedding, cross-view context) rebuilds them with the original features as self-supervision; +10.3 % mAP with the back camera missing on PETRv2. Same family as SafeMap's G-PVR and, like it, works on per-view image features, which our cached fused raster does not contain; detection only. Not relevant; SafeMap's BEV distillation is the part that transfers.

Compares softmax entropy, ensembles, MC dropout and evidential heads for BEV segmentation uncertainty and adds an uncertainty-focal cross-entropy (ECE 0.00332 against 0.00887 on LSS); the Gu et al. papers add per-vertex uncertainty and direct BEV feature use. Touches A8: an evidential head on our cached logits would give a learned per-cell unreliable signal beside the label-free heat monitor, with no extra inference time (ensembles 147 ms, dropout 457 ms against 51 - 56 ms). Blockers: camera BEV, no proof it tracks occlusion or range, extra training. Watch.

Keeps a DINOv2 image encoder frozen, adds LoRA to the attention projections and decodes with a SimpleBEV head; on nuScenes-C the ViT-L variant beats SimpleBEV by at least 20 % relative on most corruptions and holds up in darkness, but is no better for camera crash or frame loss. The result that a stronger image foundation helps night and fog but not lost cameras matches our own failure fine-tuning finding. Blocker: needs a trainable image front end; our foundation is frozen and cached. Not relevant.

Closed-form (analytic) classifiers avoid forgetting in continual test-time adaptation, and a dynamic late-fusion mechanism picks reliable modalities at test time under multi-modal corruption. It touches A8 only loosely: late fusion by reliability resembles a gate, but the page names no tasks and shows no results, and the heads are classification-style, not dense lane maps. Not relevant; abstract-level read only.

Gives each BN layer one learnable mixing coefficient between source and test statistics and optimises only those online by entropy minimisation with a two-stage KL filter (batch 1, nuScenes-C, BEVFormer); Low Light 0.3212 -> 0.3469, while TENT (0.2070) and AdaBN (0.0772) fall far below the baseline at batch 1. Warns that our adaptive-BN gain (+0.04) on the lane head may be fragile and offers a safer mixing variant. Blockers: camera detection, code not released, small gains. Watch; test the mixing variant if the +0.04 proves unstable.

Three reliability-weighted fusions: ReSMap weights camera and satellite BEV by each branch's own per-pixel prediction confidence (no router), ReliFusion feeds per-modality confidence into cross-attention, RoCaRS uses dynamic input dropout and bidirectional refinement for camera-radar segmentation. ReSMap's confidence weight is a published template for turning our hard hold (take the previous input where its heat is higher) into a smooth blend. Blockers: abstract-level reads, no ReSMap numbers, RoCaRS unverified (see RB10). Watch.

Analyses five kinds of radar noise and adds a 3D Gaussian Expansion that spreads each radar return with a kernel controlled by RCS and velocity priors, plus a weather-adaptive fusion that weights radar against camera by an estimated camera confidence map. Radar position and RCS noise are failure types we never tested (we only switch radar off), so the recipe could extend the A8 failure set, though radar adds little to lane geometry. Blockers: detection, abstract-level read, no numbers, code announced only. Watch; low priority.

An EfficientNet-B2 predicts degradation presence, severity for 12 modes, a spatial map and a health index with Healthy / Degraded / Critical bands; the index correlates 0.95 with detector mAP on failures and warns 0.47 severity units before a YOLOv8n failure (2.27 ms at 224 x 224). Relates to our label-free heat monitor (A8): it needs RGB and was trained on synthetic KITTI degradations, so it is no drop-in, but the evaluation idea (correlation with downstream failure, lead time) is directly usable. Watch; copy the protocol.

Equalises the channel counts of camera and LiDAR BEV features and fuses with an operator that reduces to identity when one sensor is absent (average, max, cross-attention); every training scene appears as L+C, L-only and C-only in shuffled mini-batches through one shared head. The 'all availability subsets in every batch' trick maps to our failure training with cached feature sets per failure type; the operator itself needs separable sensor BEV. Blockers: LiDAR-camera detection, overview-level read, no code. Watch.

Adds a camera branch to a frozen LiDAR + 4D-radar detector and predicts a per-pixel reliability map that gates camera features, trained with pseudo labels from feature similarity between projected LiDAR-radar voxels and image features (a fully occluded camera equals the baseline, 59.0 APBEV). A cell-wise reliability map with two-sensor agreement as supervision is a natural home for our label-free heat monitor. Blockers: needs LiDAR and sensor-separable streams that our fused raster lacks; missing sensors not handled. Watch.

For spatial-cross-attention BEV detectors it predicts a per-camera gated 2D offset per query to correct wrong projections under extrinsic perturbation, with clean-teacher / perturbed-student BEV-consistency training (five-camera stress test 39.69 % NDS against 28.00 for BEVFormer). It touches the extrinsic part of A8, but the repair sits inside the image-to-BEV transform, which is frozen in our foundation; the portable piece, the BEV-consistency loss, duplicates SafeMap's distillation. Not relevant; abstract-level read.

Camera-radar BEV segmentation with a radar-aware backbone, Dynamic Input Dropout and Bidirectional Feature Refinement that fills the missing branch from the present one; snippets claim +23.2 mIoU for the map without cameras and 99 % of radar-only performance. Same sensor pair and task family as ours (A8, A1), the only camera-radar map-segmentation failure paper found. Blockers: link not verified, snippet-level evidence only, radar-aware backbone rather than a frozen foundation. Watch; locate the real paper before relying on any detail.

Learns the image-to-BEV mapping without intrinsics or extrinsics (position-aware enhancement, view-aware attention; 49.7 NDS on the nuScenes leaderboard), so noisy calibration cannot hurt. It touches the extrinsic part of A8, but the projection lives inside our frozen GaussianCaR foundation and cannot be swapped; the claimed stability under extrinsic noise comes from an unopened search snippet. Not relevant: detection, replaces the encoder.

LightDiff enhances dark camera images with a diffusion model conditioned on a degraded image, LiDAR-derived depth and text; DualCross transfers LiDAR knowledge to a camera-only monocular BEV model for cross-domain use. Both are image-level night fixes (A8), but they would put raw images and a diffusion pass in front of the frozen cached foundation and add latency, against our speed rule; evidence is abstract-level without numbers. Not relevant.

A frozen Retinex-style illumination estimator gates enhancement, scales deformable offsets in 2D sampling and weights BEV residuals along vertical columns for nighttime occupancy (Occ3D-nuScenes night mIoU 19.27 with one frame; 4.7 FPS, 64.39 M parameters). For night robustness (A8) it is only a lesson: generic low-light preprocessors gave +0.08 to +0.37 mIoU, so illumination priors must enter the sampling, which sits in the image-side encoder we cannot change. Not relevant.

Serialises a road graph as an integer sequence with three decoders (autoregressive, semi- and non-autoregressive) and introduces landmark and reachability metrics for forks and merges (K47, the origin of our J). The decoders are unusable (tokens, argmax, Hungarian key points), but the metrics are evaluation-only; the extraction finds the code scores all nodes, many-to-one, skipping frames, so re-implement rather than copy. Also a frozen-encoder precedent. Use: add a fork and merge F1 curve over 0.5 to 6 m next to J, then directed reachability.

Benchmark for lane-centre-line topology on nuScenes (subset B) and Argoverse with DET_l (Frechet-distance AP at 1, 2, 3 m) and TOP_ll (adjacency AP among matched lanes). It gives a literature-facing number for our graph from about 300 lines of NumPy; scores depend on the devkit version (TopoNet TOP_ll 4.1 against 10.9 on subset A). Blockers: whole-curve matching punishes short correct lanes and ignores sparsity; a 7.7 GB annotation download needs the user's OK. Use: port the metric, score the stored champion once, quote the devkit version.

Shows that random scene splits on nuScenes leak location: 79 % of val and 86 % of test samples lie within 5 m of a training sample, and end-to-end map models lose 20 to 46 mAP on geographically disjoint splits. Our splits are scene-disjoint but never checked for location overlap; the audit is about three hours of numpy on cached ego poses, plus scores stratified by distance to TRAIN. Limit: the foundation's own exposure stays. Use: run the location-overlap audit now and report the far-bin result.

Collects nuScenes radar facts: five 77 GHz radars, sparse points with Doppler, no usable height, and a derived lateral resolution of about 1.3 m at 24 m and 2.8 m at 50 m in near mode. Radar reflects structure (vehicles, guardrails), not road paint, so single points cannot place a centre-line; this explains why radar adds little to our lane geometry and why far rays rely on the camera path. Raw radar is not cached. Context: background for A1 and censoring.

Shows that on nuScenes a model with only past ego motion and a command matches perception planners on L2, so open-loop L2 mostly measures ego status; adds a curb-collision rate (CCR) against rasterised road boundaries. It touches A7 and A9: the planner consumer E117 should be reported with an ego-status ablation, a boundary metric and a turning subset. Limit: the nuScenes command is derived from future ego motion, as is our route label. Use: add ego-status-off and CCR-like checks to the planner evaluation (K49, K108).

Benchmark of 29 camera and lidar corruptions (camera crash, frame lost, dark, blur, snow) for online map models with metrics mCE and mRR; temporal fusion lifts StreamMapNet mRR from 47.1 to 55.5, except under snow. Its corruptions map directly onto our night, blur and cameras-off set (E57, E79, E80) and support the temporal hold. Blockers: camera and lidar only, no radar, vector maps rather than lane graphs. Use: report a corrupted-over-clean ratio in the style of mRR next to our failure scores.

Non-reactive simulation that scores a 4 s plan from a recorded frame with PDMS (collision, drivable area, progress, time-to-collision, comfort); an ego-status MLP already reaches 65.6 against 84.0 for TransFuser, a second ego-status caveat (K108). It uses nuPlan and OpenScene data, gives agents no map input and needs drivable-area polygons, so it cannot score our nuScenes graph directly. Watch: re-implement drivable-area and direction compliance as graph-sensitive scores if a planner-aware metric is built.

Derived card, not a paper: a calibration-only mask of BEV cells a camera sees with usable ground sampling distance (about d squared over f times h: 0.30 m at 24 m, 1.3 m at 50 m), so rays beyond it are right-censored in the survival loss. It needs no lidar and can be precomputed; it is untested and misses vehicle occlusion and non-flat ground. It completes the hazard with censoring (K41). Use: re-implement with the foundation's crop and choose the limit on VAL.

Frame-pair stability benchmark for online maps: elements are paired through ground truth, the earlier one is moved by ego pose, and presence, localisation and shape (turning angle) are combined into mAS; accuracy and stability turn out largely independent. Our temporal consistency metric has no definition, and this gives one for K46 on matched pieces. Blockers: written for ordered polylines that are functions of x, pairing by Hungarian per frame, toolkit release unchecked. Use: adapt it on our piece graph to score the time recursion.

Defines BEV visibility as camera field of view AND a lidar ray passing, ignores invisible cells in loss and evaluation, and adds a small entropy-maximising term (weight 0.001) there. It is a template for censoring unobserved samples (A9, survival loss), but the lidar-ray condition cannot be built from calibration alone, so SN13 replaces it. Context: explains why we mask by calibration and not by lidar; the entropy term is optional, no action.

Judges perception by how much its detections change a planner's output, using a KL divergence between planner outputs on predicted and GT inputs; humans sided with it in 79 % of disagreements. The note read only the abstract (formula from memory) and it concerns detections, not lanes. Same principle as our oracle-versus-predicted swaps (E117, E119), which already show small gaps. Context: background for planner-aware evaluation; no action.

Derives soft BEV visibility from a depth distribution per camera ray and splits nuScenes val BEV into visible (66.9 %) and occluded (33.1 %) cells; lane IoU is 41.9 visible against 12.4 occluded for the proposed model. It shows that about a third of the BEV is unobserved and lane evidence there is weak, which motivates a visibility multiplier on survival terms. Blocker: needs depth distributions or lidar depth, not calibration only. Context: supports the censoring design; no action.

Pseudo-simulation: score the plan on real frames plus pre-rendered synthetic start states around the expert endpoint (EPDMS); it correlates with nuPlan closed loop at r = 0.89, with map-sensitive terms driving-direction compliance, lane keeping and drivable area. It gives ready definitions of graph-sensitive planner scores (open item 5 of the overview), but needs nuPlan data and a Gaussian-splat rendering pipeline. Watch: reuse the sub-score definitions if a planner-aware metric for lane graphs is built.

For radar-to-BEV occupancy, supervises only cells the lidar could observe and counts occupied predictions in unobservable cells as an unknown-region hallucination rate. This pair (loss mask plus hallucination metric) is what censoring needs on A9, with the lidar part replaced by the SN13 calibration mask plus box shadows. Blockers: the authors' own campus data, not nuScenes; mask built from lidar; no numbers seen. Watch: add the hallucination-rate metric once an observability mask exists.

Synthesis card, not a paper: evaluate a map or graph by swapping the input of one fixed consumer (GT, predicted, region-masked, perturbed, shuffled) and report the swap gap, with an ego-status-off variant so the consumer cannot ignore the graph. We did part of this (oracle route 0.316 m against 0.34 m in E119; graph A against B in E117) and gaps were small, as in the literature. Blocker: consumers that use ego status hide the gap. Watch: extend with masked and perturbed inputs for the planner-aware metric.

Collection of metric definitions from growth papers: junction metric, TOPO, shortest-path agreement, landmark and reachability, SDA, point and branch F1 with one-to-one matching, Betti errors, StreetMover. Our split and merge F1 at 6 m already is a landmark metric, so this is a lookup for definitions; the usable tolerance curve comes from RNTR (GR14). Note has little detail beyond the definitions. Context: background for A9; no action.

Argues for predicting whole survival distributions and testing them with D-calibration (predicted survival at the event time should be uniform, with a rule for censored cases); medical data. It could give a probability-integral-transform check of our endpoint law P(k) on labelled rays, touching calibration of per-vertex probabilities (open item 4); note read the abstract only, formula from memory. Blocker: ties in the discrete ring grid need randomisation. Watch: try it if hazard calibration is examined.

Surveys how to say 'the model could not see this' instead of 'the lane ended': Occ3D ray-cast lidar and camera visibility, PanopticBEV occlusion as a class, learned per-point visibility heads (Anchor3DLane, LATR). For us only the calibration frustum mask and an occluder-shadow mask from a vehicle layer work without lidar; lidar-derived labels would bring lidar into the label pipeline. Context: background for the censoring design; SN13 holds the concrete recipe.

Distils a teacher that sees four future BEV frames into a single-frame student (BEV feature L2 plus query-logit KL) to improve the road ahead, and reports ahead and rear mAP. A recursion that sees past and future could teach a causal student from our sequences, which works on cached BEV (A5). Blockers: logit distillation uses Hungarian matching, MapTracker-based teacher, no code, camera only. Watch: privileged-future teacher for the time recursion, later.

Closed-loop planning benchmark with about 1,500 h of human driving in four cities and a lightweight simulator; the route is a roadblock-id sequence and the map a lane graph. Scoring needs nuPlan logs and maps, not our nuScenes frames, and the note read the abstract only. Not relevant: out of scope (dataset); only its metric families serve as a template, no next step.

title: Beyond Chamfer Distance: Granular Order-aware Evaluation Metric For Online Mapping
text: SOSPA aligns polylines of different vertex counts by a monotone edit-distance DP, so it can score our sparse vertex chains against dense ground truth and punishes superfluous vertices, which fits our short-and-correct rule. PLD uses Hungarian assignment but only as a metric, and its split shows detection, not geometry, is the bottleneck. It runs on the Lilja geographic nuScenes split. Use: re-implement SOSPA for lane pieces as a report metric next to S and Q; code is announced, not released.
idea: Proposes SOSPA, an order-aware polyline similarity solved by dynamic programming that allows unmatched points, and PLD, a confidence-weighted multi-instance score with a localisation / detection split, evaluated on the geographically disjoint nuScenes split.

title: Failure Modes for Deep Learning-Based Online Mapping: How to Measure and Address Them
text: Extends the Lilja leakage work with a geometry axis: how new a scene layout is, not only how far away it is. It gives a threshold-free per-element Frechet statistic and a way to test whether the seen-versus-unseen gap of our foundation (0.932 against 0.820) is location or geometry. Camera models only, no code on the page. Use: re-implement the geometric-novelty split on our VAL and TEST scenes and report S against novelty.
idea: Separates feature memorisation from layout overfitting with splits controlled for geographic and geometric similarity, Frechet-distance statistics, two overfitting scores and a minimum-spanning-tree diversity and coverage measure on nuScenes and Argoverse 2 (CVPR 2026).

title: Rethinking Training & Inference for Forecasting: Linking Winner-Take-All back to GMMs
text: Names the over-segmentation and unstable assignment of hard WTA that show up as duplicate or blurred children at a fork. The EM step needs no retraining and could calibrate the child scores that rank our b hypotheses; the merge step is a matching-free duplicate remover. Blocker: trajectory forecasting with Gaussian modes, no code on the page. Use: try the EM responsibilities on the child scores of a trained tip.
idea: Shows that winner-take-all forecasters are trained like K-means but read as Gaussian mixtures, which makes mode probabilities uninformative, and fixes it post hoc by test-time merging of nearby modes and one EM step with soft responsibilities shared across neighbouring modes (ECCV 2026).

title: Annealed Winner-Takes-All for Motion Forecasting
text: First use of annealed multiple choice learning on a driving-scale structured predictor (UniTraj / MTR), so it is the closest published test of our aMCL arm for the b children of a tip. The loss is stand-alone (awta_loss and temperature_scheduler) and Apache-2.0, so porting costs little. Blocker: forecasting trajectories, not geometric trees, and one GT continuation per tip gives no split. Use: take the scheduler as the reference implementation for the aMCL cooling arm.
idea: Applies the annealed WTA loss (temperature-cooled softmin over hypotheses) to state-of-the-art motion forecasting models and shows it improves minimum-error metrics with few hypotheses and no post-selection.

title: ModeSeq: Taming Sparse Multimodal Motion Prediction with Sequential Mode Modeling
text: A different answer to duplicates and starvation than WTA variants: later duplicates of a matched mode become negatives, so the second child is pushed to another continuation. It could replace the share-0.1 relaxed WTA arm as a duplicate-suppressing label for the b children, with a distance threshold as match test. Blockers: needs a match criterion and a decoding order, trajectory forecasting only, no code on the page. Watch: sketch EMTA on the child ring.
idea: Decodes the modes of a multimodal prediction one after another so each depends on the earlier ones, and trains with Early-Match-Take-All, which labels the earliest matching mode positive and later matches negative, with focal-loss confidences (CVPR 2025).

title: TopoMaskV3: 3D Mask Head with Dense Offset and Height Predictions for Road Topology Understanding
text: A second follow-up of the Lilja leakage finding on OpenLane-V2: the original split is inflated (a Bezier model drops to 27.8 on Near), and the mask representation loses less under geographic shift. Its dense mask plus offset head is the nearest relative of our dense head, and its splits are a test bed for topology metrics. Blockers: camera / lidar encoder, Argoverse data, no code, release of split lists not confirmed. Watch: reuse the split recipe if lists appear.
idea: Extends a dense-mask centreline method with sub-cell offset and per-cell height heads, and replaces the OpenLane-V2 subset-A split by geographically disjoint Near and Far splits plus a +-100 m benchmark (CVPR 2026 workshop).

title: CRISP: A Spatiotemporal Camera-Radar Backbone for Driving via Forecasting-Based World-Model Pretraining
text: A second camera-radar BEV foundation next to GaussianCaR, with radar-aware temporal self-attention and modality gating. Its nuScenes map table (split not stated) gives lane IoU 35.4 and divider IoU 29.3 against 31.3 and 25.7 for UniAD, but the downstream heads are trained and it is not stated as frozen. No code (project page only), under review. Watch: if weights appear, export its BEV as a second frozen raster and compare lane F1 with GaussianCaR.
idea: Camera-radar BEV backbone pretrained by forecasting future lidar point clouds (lidar only in pretraining), then transferred to detection, tracking, online mapping, motion forecasting, occupancy and planning on nuScenes.

title: The Road Ahead in Autonomous Driving: The KITScenes Multimodal Dataset
text: A public set with radar, cameras and a full lane map, so it could test a radar-camera foundation and our graph head on new cities and sensors. Its map benchmark reports AP for lane centerlines and a topology AP with MapTRv2, SDTagNet and MapQR-Topo. Blockers: 4D imaging radar differs from nuScenes radar, the dataset is CC BY-NC 4.0 with extra terms, the early release is not meant for final reporting, splits not seen. Watch: read the topology score definition when the full release arrives.
idea: A European multimodal dataset with three 4D imaging radars, cameras, 400 m lidar and Lanelet2 HD maps over 62 km2 with topology, plus four benchmarks including online HD map construction (5.7 h, 162 km, three cities).
licence: Apache-2.0 (code); dataset CC BY-NC 4.0 plus KITScenes terms

title: UBD-Bench: Benchmarking and Analyzing Unimodal Branch Degradation in Multimodal Perception for Autonomous Driving
text: A protocol for judging frozen BEV features with matched small decoders, the same setting as our cached raster, covering online map construction and BEV map segmentation. It suggests auditing the camera branch of a camera-radar foundation against its own camera-only training. Blockers: camera and lidar models only, so a radar branch audit is open; no code on the page. Watch: copy the matched-probe protocol to compare cached BEV variants of GaussianCaR.
idea: A benchmark with a Paired Frozen-Branch Probe that trains identical decoders on frozen branch features of unimodal-trained versus jointly-trained models, finds camera branches degrade after multimodal training (most at the pre-fusion camera BEV), and repairs it by unimodal-to-multimodal distillation.

title: Differentiable Knapsack and Top-k Operators via Dynamic Programming
text: Entropy-smoothed DP top-k is a principled alternative to SOFT top-k for passing gradient to dropped hypotheses in the per-tip selection of b children from M tips, and the knapsack form could encode a vertex budget. Shannon entropy is shown to be the only permutation-equivariant regulariser. Blocker: tested on decision-focused learning and RL, not perception; no code on the page. Watch: re-implement on the M x b scores as an ablation next to SOFT top-k.
idea: Casts knapsack and top-k as dynamic programs and smooths the recursions to get differentiable operators with deterministic and stochastic forward passes and parallel vector-Jacobian products.

title: Multiple Choice Learning for Efficient Speech Separation with Many Speakers
text: A concrete case where MCL replaces assignment-based set matching (PIT) with equal quality and cheaper training, which supports our no-matching rule for set outputs. The authors suggest extending it to a variable number of sources, which is our case of a variable number of children. Blockers: audio, fixed source count, no code on the page. Watch: cite as evidence that MCL can stand in for matching; no experiment needed.
idea: Replaces permutation-invariant training for speech separation by multiple choice learning and matches its quality on WSJ0-mix and LibriMix at lower compute.

title: Mode-as-Sequence: Translating Multimodal Motion Prediction into Unified Sequential Mode Modeling
text: Same EMTA label as ModeSeq, plus a one-pass parallel decoder that matters for ms per frame when b grows, and a ranking regulariser for confidences that need only be ranked, not normalised. First place in two Waymo challenges. Blockers: trajectory forecasting, no code on the page. Context: read only if the EMTA arm of ModeSeq is built.
idea: Extends ModeSeq with a parallel variant that keeps mode dependencies through masked attention but decodes all modes in one pass, a joint-scene Early-Match-Take-All and a ranking regulariser.

title: Principled Top-k Selection for Language Models with Hybrid Gradients
text: States our gap exactly: plain top-k gradient only adjusts weights of the chosen items, not which of m candidates is chosen. The policy-gradient part is an exploration term for non-selected candidates, which our selection with gradient through the selected items lacks. Blockers: language-model tasks, policy-gradient variance, no code. Watch: read the method for a variance-reduced exploration term; context for the selection ablation.
idea: Trains a top-k selector with a gradient that mixes a supervised part and a policy-gradient part, with an O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence rate, tested on synthetic regression, RAG and mixture-of-experts.

title: LaPrune: Controllable Differentiable Sparsity at Million Scale
text: Exact budget control with a hardness knob that is unaffected by score scaling is a clean way to anneal soft selection toward hard top-M at inference, which targets the train-test mismatch of soft top-k in our builder. Blockers: aimed at million-scale pruning, no code on the page, our M is small. Watch: use the hardness schedule idea if the soft-selection ablation shows a mismatch.
idea: A differentiable top-k layer with exact budget control that keeps the selected mass fixed and moves the mask from a dense equal-mass allocation toward hard top-k with one hardness parameter.

title: Uncertainty Matters: Structured Probabilistic Online Mapping for Motion Prediction in Autonomous Driving
text: Gives vertex-level uncertainty with along-lane correlation, so a calibration check for our vertices (predicted covariance against error) becomes measurable. It is an A9 metric idea and an A8 head idea; our hazard validity is a different object from position uncertainty. Blockers: camera MapTR-style host, code promised but not linked. Watch: borrow the covariance-versus-error calibration plot for vertex position.
idea: Predicts a dense low-rank-plus-diagonal covariance over map vertices instead of a diagonal one and shows on nuScenes better online map generation and map-based motion prediction.

title: WASABI: Whole-graph Assignment-based Stabilizer for lAne topology By Inter-frame tracking
text: New: segment tracks with a state machine, an edge memory (score of each from-to pair over a 10-frame window, valid if 5 exceed a threshold) and ground-truth-anchored temporal metrics (connection toggle rate, label flicker). Closest published relative of our time recursion on a graph with explicit edges; the window vote is a hard version of log-odds validity. Blockers: Hungarian per heading group, rule-based, 16 internal sequences, unnamed in-house BEV model, no code. Verdict use: copy toggle rate and flicker as metrics, re-implement the window vote as an edge-memory baseline.
idea: A real-time post-processing stabiliser that tracks lane segments and their connectivity jointly across frames (10 Hz, 20 ms, up to 200 lanes) and reports connectivity toggle rate and label flicker on 16 internal sequences.

title: Uncertainty-Instructed Structure Injection for Generalizable HD Map Construction
text: An early use of the Lilja geographic splits for a method claim, with uncertainty-driven resampling as the generalisation device. Little for us: the gain comes from a perspective-view branch and a trainable decoder, and the code is promised but not confirmed. Context: shows that geographic splits are now the standard way to evaluate.
idea: Resamples from uncertainty-based distributions and distils explicit instance prompts into a map decoder for generalisation, reporting +5.7 mAP on geographically disjoint nuScenes splits.

title: Impact of Localization Errors on Label Quality for Online HD Map Construction
text: Finds that heading error hurts more than position error and that performance falls more than linearly with the share of noisy labels, which matters for any label pipeline built from a map and poses. A distance-binned score is an easy add to our report. Blockers: camera MapTRv2 only, no code. Context: use the noise model to stress our labels, not as a method.
idea: Models ramp, Gaussian and Perlin localisation noise in fleet-projected labels, trains MapTRv2 on Argoverse 2 at several error levels and proposes a distance-based evaluation metric.

title: Systematic Discovery of Semantic Attacks in Online Map Construction through Conditional Diffusion
text: A rare study that measures map faults by their effect on planning, which supports a planner-consequence metric for false and missing lanes. The attack is camera-only and semantic, so it does not touch our frozen radar-camera raster, and there is no code. Context: motivates better-short-than-false with planner numbers; no action.
idea: Uses diffusion-generated plausible environment changes (shadows, wet roads) that keep the topology but make online map models remove or inject boundaries on nuScenes; boundary removal corrupts 96 percent of planned trajectories.

title: Towards Reliable Evaluation of Road Network Reconstructions
text: Older paper the earlier searches missed: common road-network metrics can rank algorithms inconsistently. For graph-based lane evaluation it is a reference for a cross-check between several metrics on our own graphs, next to TOPO, JTOPO and S. The page gives no code and no detail of the three metrics beyond the abstract. Context: read the full paper before adding a metric.
idea: Shows that common road-network metrics are blind to whole categories of errors and proposes three new metrics that compare ground-truth and reconstructed networks in different ways yet agree with each other.

title: Fast LapSum: Exact Differentiable Top-k at Million Scale
text: Exact-k soft top-k with end-to-end gradient, built for 10^6 and more scores; our selection runs on a few hundred scores per frame, so the speed trick is not needed, but the exact-mass property could replace the two-anchor transport of SOFT top-k. Blocker: no code on the page, speed focus is not our problem. Context only; LapSum itself is the thing to use if a soft top-k arm is built.
idea: Scalable solver for the LapSum soft top-k that keeps the selected mass exactly k, with probabilistic bracketing and a certification pass; demonstrated on adversarial examples and Gaussian-splatting densification.

title: Diffsurv: Differentiable sorting for censored time-to-event data
text: The one item that joins censoring with differentiable ordering: censored labels yield a set of consistent permutations, the same structure as rays that leave the observable area while the hazard orders failures. It could supply a ranking loss on ray-survival times that tolerates censoring. Blockers: tabular healthcare risk, permutation matrices are costly, no code. Context: keep as a backup for censoring-aware calibration of the verifier.
idea: Extends differentiable sorting to censored time-to-event data by predicting matrices of possible permutations that encode the label uncertainty of censoring, and derives a top-k risk predictor.

title: Shiva-DiT: Residual-Based Differentiable Top-k Selection for Efficient Diffusion Transformers
text: A straight-through top-k whose gradient reaches the scores and the budget k itself, relevant to our learned sparsity budget (vertices per 100 m) and to the train-test mismatch of soft selection. Blockers: diffusion-transformer token pruning, no code on the page. Context: copy the idea of learning k under an average-budget constraint if the keep-gate penalty proves hard to balance.
idea: Hard top-k in the forward pass with a residual-aware straight-through estimator that sends gradient to both token scores and the budget k, with learned retention schedules under a target average budget.

title: Beyond Hungarian: Match-Free Supervision for End-to-End Object Detection
text: A 2026 match-free DETR loss in line with our rule, but the correspondence is learned inside a query decoder and still pairs one ground truth with one query, so it does not address crowded cases such as parallel lanes. Blockers: object detection on COCO, no code on the page, numbers not verified. Context: our MCL-style losses are simpler; no action.
idea: A DETR training method without explicit matching: encoded ground truth queries the decoder through cross-attention and the learned correspondences supervise the queries, cutting matching latency by over 50 percent.

title: CaR1: A Multi-Modal Baseline for BEV Vehicle Segmentation via Camera-Radar Fusion
text: From the GaussianCaR group; vehicle class only, so it adds nothing for lane maps, but its grid radar encoding and adaptive fusion weights are cheap alternatives to the radar branch of a foundation. The repository is a refactoring stub with LICENSE and README only. Context: nothing to do now.
idea: Camera-radar BEV vehicle segmentation built on BEVFusion with a grid-based radar encoding and an adaptive fusion step, 57.6 IoU on nuScenes.

title: Beyond Endpoints: Path-Centric Reasoning for Vectorized Off-Road Network Extraction
text: New: path-centric edge evidence (WildRoad F1 78.85 against 76.74 for SAM-Road++); a fast variant is stated as 2.5x faster. Touches our ray verifier and link head: the path statistics over the heat map are a cheap verifier input and the source-competition bias suits fork mouths. Blockers: aerial imagery, SAM encoder, NMS vertices. Verdict use; next step: add the 9-dimensional path feature to the ray verifier as baseline B3.
idea: MaGRoad scores every candidate edge from 32 samples of multi-scale pooled road probability along the whole segment (mean, std, softmin) with a competition bias among edges of one source, instead of reading only the two endpoints.

title: Widest-Path Reachability Fields for Connectivity-Preserving Slender Structure Segmentation
text: New (Jul 2026): a loss aimed at the few bottleneck pixels that decide connectivity (called topological gradient starvation), without skeletonisation or homology; stated to improve 87 percent of experiments and clDice by 7.2 points on fragile sets. Touches the dense head: broken heat-map lines at junction mouths and occlusions get gradient where pixel losses give almost none. Blockers: dynamic programming cost at 200x200 unknown, mask targets, no code. Verdict watch; next step: read the method and compare with TRACE and clDice.
idea: WPRF is a differentiable max-min reachability objective computed by dynamic programming on a domain-restricted graph, with a bottleneck-aware term, that keeps thin curvilinear structures connected at no inference overhead.

title: TRACE: Topology-Aware Reconnection via Prediction-Adaptive Connectivity Enforcement for Thin-Structure Segmentation
text: New (WACV 2027): connectivity supervision that follows the model's own cheapest reconnection instead of fixed skeleton locations, over six 2D and 3D benchmarks (no numbers on the page). Touches the dense head: lane heat maps break at occlusions and junction mouths, and a bottleneck-path term supervises those gaps without matching. Blockers: built for masks, differentiability not stated, code only after acceptance. Verdict watch; next step: re-read when code appears.
idea: Training objective for thin-structure segmentation that uses a target skeleton to define required local connections, finds the easiest valid reconnection under the current prediction and supervises that route's bottleneck together with the matching skeleton point.

title: clDice - A Novel Topology-Preserving Loss Function for Tubular Structure Segmentation
text: Older work missing from the catalogue: a connectivity loss built from soft skeletons, tested on five public sets with better connectivity and graph similarity. Touches the dense head: an extra term that keeps centre-lines connected, and soft-skeleton pooling is a differentiable thinning operator toward the graph builder. Blockers: binary masks (our target is a Gaussian heat map, so a threshold is needed), extra compute, no code on the page. Verdict watch; next step: one A/B arm on the thresholded heat map.
idea: centerlineDice measures overlap between masks and their morphological skeletons and provably preserves topology up to homotopy equivalence, with soft-clDice as a differentiable and efficient loss (CVPR 2021).

title: Skeleton Recall Loss for Connectivity Conserving and Resource Efficient Segmentation of Thin Tubular Structures
text: Older work missing from the catalogue: a topology loss without soft skeletonisation, reported to cut computational overhead by more than 90 percent against other topology-focused losses. Touches the dense head as a cheaper alternative to clDice; skeleton targets could be precomputed offline from our ground-truth graphs. Blockers: written for masks, not heat maps; no code link on the page. Verdict watch; next step: only if clDice shows a gain.
idea: Connectivity loss for thin tubular structures that shifts most of the work to inexpensive CPU operations and is presented as the first multi-class capable loss of its kind (ECCV 2024).

title: GSMap: 2D Gaussians for Online HD Mapping
text: New: Gaussians as vertex carriers with a differentiable rasteriser giving pixel-level constraints; nuScenes and Argoverse2 gains are reported but the page has no numbers or FPS. Touches the open gap of gradient between graph and dense raster (sibling of MapVR) and our soft-rasteriser idea. Blockers: plugs into camera map architectures whose decoders were not checked, preprint, code announced. Verdict watch; next step: read the rasteriser when code is out.
idea: Represents each map element as an ordered sequence of learnable 2D Gaussians centred on polyline vertices, trained with differentiable rasterisation plus a topology-aware vectorisation component.

title: When Should a Network Emit Geometry, and When Should It Detect It? Readout, Reconciliation, and Representation in Floorplan Vectorization
text: Evidence from a neighbouring domain: on CubiCasa5K detection beats sequence decoding on every wall metric (about +2.7 wall F1, paired bootstrap excluding zero), the advantage grows with plan size, and deterministic fusion of both outputs adds about 7 wall F1. Supports our dense-then-sparse choice against token decoders and shows a paired-bootstrap protocol. Blockers: floorplans, not lanes; no transfer test. Verdict context; no action.
idea: Compares emitting floorplan geometry as an autoregressive coordinate sequence with detecting junctions and centerlines on dense heat maps and assembling them into a graph.

title: PseudoMapLabeler: Confidence-Aware Pseudo-Label Generation for Semi-Supervised Online Mapping
text: New (ECCV 2026 DriveX workshop): spatial clipping keeps the high-confidence parts of an element and removes the rest, +6.1 mAP in a low-label nuScenes regime. Touches our rule of better short than false and the time recursion (confidence from repeated observations), and it is a label-efficiency recipe for A9. Blockers: camera mapping hosts, no code, not a dense-head method. Verdict watch; next step: borrow the Beta confidence over frames as a validity target. A5 angle (search 2026-10-25): per BEV cell and class a Beta posterior over a scene (alpha from calibrated, ego-warped teacher scores, beta from missed observations) is a bounded alternative to the log-odds evidence of L2G-Map.
idea: Teacher-student framework that builds pseudo-labels for online HD mapping, estimating per-element reliability with Beta-distribution confidence maps over temporal observations and clipping unreliable segments instead of dropping whole elements.

title: Improving Online Lane Graph Extraction by Object-Lane Clustering
text: Older work missing from the catalogue: direct object-to-lane supervision that works with the outputs of any detector at test time. Touches the dense head: detected vehicles with positions and headings are cheap evidence of lane centres where markings are missing, if an object or radar-detection channel is available. Blockers: needs a detector, camera lane-graph host, abstract gives no datasets or numbers, no code. Verdict watch; next step: test an object cue on the dense head.
idea: Uses 3D object detection outputs to improve online lane graph estimation by treating centerlines as cluster centres and objects as data points with a learned soft assignment (ICCV 2023).

title: CAPE: Connectivity-Aware Path Enforcement Loss for Curvilinear Structure Delineation
text: New (Apr 2025): graph-aware connectivity loss from shortest paths between ground-truth node pairs, evaluated on neuron and blood-vessel tracing with topology-aware metrics (no numbers on the page). Touches the dense head and our graph metrics: it penalises false links as well as breaks, which fits the rule better short than false. Blockers: roads and lanes not mentioned, differentiability and cost not stated, no code. Verdict watch; next step: none until WPRF or TRACE has been tested.
idea: Connectivity loss for curvilinear structures: node pairs are chosen from the ground-truth graph, matching paths are found in the predicted segmentation by a shortest-path algorithm, and both broken and false-positive connections are penalised.

title: TopoMaskV2: Enhanced Instance-Mask-Based Formulation for the Road Topology Problem
text: Older work missing from the catalogue (the catalogue holds TopoMask inside the RoadPainter note): OLS rises from 44.1 to 49.4 on subset A and 44.7 to 51.8 on subset B. Touches the dense head: four direction labels on a mask are a coarse relative of our direction channels, and mask-to-centerline conversion is the dense-to-sparse step. Blockers: camera encoder, rule-based post-processing, no code. Verdict context; no action.
idea: Represents lane centerlines as instance masks with a masked-attention transformer, adds a four-direction label encoding that gives mask instances flow information and converts masks to centerlines by post-processing.

title: GraphMorph: Tubular Structure Extraction by Morphing Predicted Graphs
text: Dense-plus-graph hybrid for vessels and roads: branch-level instead of pixel-level reasoning, and the graph removes false positives of the segmentation. Touches the dense head and graph builder, but the page gives no numbers and no statement on differentiability, and code is only announced. Blockers: patch-level graph decoder with unknown matching, Dijkstra step is a rule. Verdict context; no action.
idea: A Graph Decoder predicts a branch-level graph per image patch from segmentation features and a Morph Module combines it with the centerline probability map through SkeletonDijkstra to output a centerline mask aligned with the graph (NeurIPS 2024).

title: TopoCurve: Geometry-Aware Topology Reasoning via Bezier Curves in Autonomous Driving
text: New: analytic tangents and endpoint distance from the Bezier curve feed the link scoring; 50.6 OLS without post-processing and 56.8 DET_p against 52.6, as stated. Touches the link head: tangent alignment plus endpoint distance resembles TopoLogic and CoPo, and one-to-many branches ease matching pressure. Blockers: multi-view camera encoder, OpenLane-V2 only, no code. Verdict context; no action beyond noting tangent-aware link scores.
idea: Models each lane as an endpoint-fixed cubic Bezier curve and reuses the curve geometry for Fourier-feature topology encodings, deformable cross-attention guidance and parallel curve-anchored branches with one-to-many supervision (NeurIPS 2026).

title: SEMIR: Topology-Preserving Graph Minors for Thin-Structure Segmentation
text: New (Jun 2026): the dense raster is reduced to a small graph before learning, matching domain baselines on TTPLA, CrackSeg9k and SkyScapes Lane and cutting mask fragmentation at least 4.6x against SLIC. A sparse-graph-first idea for large rasters, while our 200x200 grid is already small. Blockers: aerial and crack data, differentiability and cost not stated, no code. Verdict context; no action.
idea: Replaces the pixel grid by a parameterised graph minor of tens to hundreds of boundary-aligned supernodes, classifies it with a lightweight GNN and lifts predictions back exactly to pixel resolution, for structures 1 to 3 pixels wide.

title: TopoHR: Hierarchical Centerline Representation for Cyclic Topology Reasoning in Driving Scenes with Point-to-Instance Relations
text: New: hierarchical centerline features and point-to-instance links; DET_l +3.8 and TOP_ll +5.4 on OpenLane-V2 subset_A over the previous best, as stated. Touches the link head only as another scoring idea; point-to-instance links resemble vertex-to-piece reasoning. Blockers: camera decoder, OpenLane-V2 only, abstract read only so matching is not checked. Verdict context; no action.
idea: End-to-end framework in which centerline detection and topology reasoning improve each other, using point queries, instance queries and a topology module with point-to-instance and instance-to-instance links (CVPR 2026).

title: GeoReFormer: Geometry-Aware Refinement for Lane Segment Detection and Topology Reasoning
text: New: bounded polyline refinement and gated topology propagation; 34.5 mAP on OpenLane-V2 as stated. Bounded refinement matches our bounded teardrop offsets and the gate resembles our keep gate, but both live in decoder queries of a camera model. Blockers: transformer queries, OpenLane-V2 only, no code on the page, abstract read only. Verdict context; no action.
idea: Adds geometry and topology biases to a lane-segment transformer decoder: data-driven geometric priors for query initialisation, bounded coordinate refinement of polylines and per-query gated topology propagation.

title: ARETE: Attention-based Rasterized Encoding for Topology Estimation using HSV-transformed Crowdsourced Vehicle Fleet Data
text: New: trajectory presence and direction encoded as a colour raster input; evaluated on an internal set plus nuScenes and nuPlan (no numbers on the page). Its direction-in-hue raster is a relative of our heat-map-plus-direction target, but the input is fleet data, not sensors. Blockers: crowdsourced trajectories, DETR decoding, no code. Verdict context; no action.
idea: DETR-based model that reads a rasterised, direction-encoded (HSV) map of crowdsourced vehicle trajectories per tile and predicts vectorised directed centerlines and lane dividers.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Sparsity and Redundancy: A Dual-Decoding Framework with Global Context for Map Inference
text: Missing from the catalogue: keypoints plus relation prediction on a rasterised grid with global context, stated as +5 percent APLS over state of the art on three trajectory datasets. Touches the graph builder: a global-context relation module is a second opinion on links where local evidence is sparse, as in SAM-Road. Blockers: trajectory input, no code. Verdict context; no action.
idea: DGMap infers road maps from trajectory data with multi-scale grid encoding, mask-enhanced keypoint extraction and global-context relation prediction to avoid fragmentation in sparse areas and false links in dense areas.

title: Dynamic Exploration on Segment-Proposal Graphs for Tubular Centerline Tracking
text: New: lazy graph construction while tracking a centerline, tested on retinal vessels, roads and rivers; the abstract claims better accuracy and efficiency but gives no numbers. Touches the verified-ray builder: evaluating only visited candidates mirrors our hypothesis tree, but it is an interactive tracker with discrete Q-learning and no gradient. Blockers: described as independent of deep learning, no code. Verdict context; no action.
idea: Builds the segment-proposal graph on demand during the search, framed as a Markov decision process, with Q-learning computing edge weights only for the transitions the search visits.

title: End-to-End Autonomous Recursive Arborescence Deformable Flow and Non-Linear Hemodynamics for Patient-Specific Coronary Centerline Extraction
text: Neighbouring domain (CT): step termination is stated to be differentiable, the full pipeline is not. Touches the builder: seeds plus recursive bifurcation with parent pointers has the structure of our hypothesis tree, but Tree-NMS is a rule step. Blockers: 3D CT volumes, a hemodynamic solver unrelated to us, no code. Verdict context; no action.
idea: Extracts coronary trees end to end: a landmark head finds start points, a deformable step-flow model samples 3D feature pyramids to generate trajectories, and a top-down recursive state machine detects bifurcations with Tree-NMS and assigns parent pointers.

title: Relationformer: A Unified Framework for Image-to-Graph Generation
text: Older work missing from the catalogue (2022): joint node and edge prediction with a relation token, state of the art on several domains, no numbers on the page. Touches the graph builder only as the standard set-based graph baseline. Blockers: direct set-based prediction (matching assumed), image input, no code on the page. Verdict not-relevant; superseded by pair-head pipelines such as SAM-Road.
idea: One-stage transformer that predicts objects and their relations jointly, with a learnable relation token next to the object tokens, for image-to-graph generation such as road networks, vessels and scene graphs.

title: MARS - A foundational map auto-regressor
text: New (14 Oct 2026): one autoregressive model for roads and buildings with a chat interface, stated to match or beat multistage baselines on four road and building datasets. Touches nothing in our chain: sequence output is the token family we avoid, and the imagery type is not stated on the page. Blockers: autoregressive decoding, no code (dataset and demo on Hugging Face). Verdict not-relevant.
idea: Map foundation model inspired by autoregressive language models that produces road networks as multiple polylines and building footprints as polygons in one process, trained on the MAP-3M dataset.

title: Distilled Roads: Generalisable Road Network Extraction Across Sensors, Resolutions, and Region
text: New (ECCV 2026 workshop): resolution-decreasing distillation curriculum; City-Scale and Global-Scale gains of up to 22 F1 and 15 APLS points and about 3x faster inference, as stated. Touches nothing in our chain except the idea of topology-aware supervision for a road-graph model. Blockers: satellite imagery only, no code. Verdict not-relevant.
idea: Treats global road extraction from satellite imagery as continual adaptation, combining cross-resolution distillation, multi-sensor training and topology-aware supervision in one model.

title: HGeo-TopoMap: Boosting Topological Mapping with Hierarchical Geometric Priors
text: New: prior-mask attention and orientation-aligned instance features; the abstract gives no numbers. The modules encode features of an inverse-perspective road-structure map with a trainable encoder, so nothing ports to a frozen BEV raster. Code and weights are announced at github.com/lynn-yu/HGeo-TopoMap. Verdict not-relevant; no action.
idea: Topological mapping on OpenLane-V2 with a geometric adaptive learning module on an inverse-perspective road-structure map and a geometric consistency module that aligns centerline instances with similar orientation.

title: RoadWeaver: Large-Scale Lane-Level HD Map Generation from Scratch for Autonomous Driving Simulation
text: New: simulation map generation with 99.8 percent reachability, 10.7 percent dead-end ratio and 0.24 m endpoint alignment error, as stated, in 1.39 to 3.50 s per map. Touches nothing in our chain: it generates synthetic maps instead of perceiving lanes. Its reachability and dead-end measures are a possible check on our graphs. Blockers: not a perception method, no code yet. Verdict not-relevant.
idea: Coarse-to-fine generation of large HD maps from scratch for simulation: global road layout, then a connected road network, then lane-level geometry with topologically consistent connectivity.

title: Odyssey: A Closed-Loop Benchmark for Long-Horizon Real-World Driving with Explicit Navigation Routes
text: First benchmark that scores route following with an SD route as the only navigation input, including lane preparation before a manoeuvre, which is our lane-level route-flag question at the consumer end. It needs 3DGS-rendered camera images and camera or VLA planners, so we cannot run it; the metrics can be copied for E117-type route tests. The route is a polyline, no abstention or wrong-map case is stated. Verdict watch: code is announced but not released, re-check later.
idea: Closed-loop benchmark of 100 scenarios rebuilt from 100-second nuPlan logs in which directional commands are replaced by explicit SD-map routes, with the new metrics SD Route Compliance, Pre-Lane Change Score and RouteDS.

title: SeqLoc: Beyond the Single Frame for Cross-View Geo-Localization in Feature-Sparse Scenes
text: Input is ground-level panoramas in rural scenes, so only the fusion logic transfers: tempering each frame volume by its entropy and mixing in a map-shaped recovery term protects a product-of-volumes registration (OrienterNet style, K99) against confident wrong frames, and belief entropy is a ready abstain signal. This ties A5 to A6; it is a recursive filter, easy to keep soft and differentiable. Pose level only, no lane level or route. Verdict use as an idea; benchmark and code on the project page.
idea: Online sequence aggregation of per-frame pose-likelihood volumes on OpenStreetMap with entropy-tempered likelihoods, a map-guided relocalisation term that recovers suppressed true poses, and sub-grid peak-anchored smoothing; the abstract reports over 50 percent better position and orientation recall than single frames.

title: Lane-Level Route Planning for Autonomous Vehicles
text: Gives a principled cost-to-go for the question of our route head: which lane to occupy now so that the next manoeuvre stays reachable, including lane-change edges and their failure risk. On our perceived graph it can generate a soft lane-level route target (expected cost per lane instead of a binary on-route flag) and a feature for E117; the search itself is a rule step, so labels only, not the training path. Hard graph, no SD uncertainty or abstention on the page, no code. Verdict use, effort S.
idea: Plans routes on a lane-level road network as an MDP with uncertain lane-change outcomes and shows that a Dijkstra-like method finds the lowest expected cost route in O(n log n), weighing when to change lanes before a manoeuvre.

title: U-BEV: Height-aware Bird's-Eye-View Segmentation and Neural Map-based Relocalization
text: Nearest published match to our no-pose-given step: a BEV raster, a U-Net style network and a differentiable template matcher against SD-map data on nuScenes, reporting over 26 percent higher recall accuracy than earlier BEV relocalisation (page figure). The pose output format is not described, no uncertainty or abstention, no lane level or route, and the camera BEV is theirs, not our frozen raster. No code on the page. Verdict watch; read the matcher before building our small pose-volume module (E103e).
idea: A U-Net-inspired BEV model that reasons over several height layers before flattening, combined with a differentiable template matcher that relocalises the neural BEV on neural SD-map data, trained end to end on nuScenes (IROS 2024).

title: SegLocNet: Multimodal Localization Network for Autonomous Driving via Bird's-Eye-View Segmentation
text: Closest in input to us: a BEV semantic raster matched exhaustively to a map, with the SD case in the same representation, so a registration front end (K99 family) on nuScenes; it is named in register line K100 but has no catalogue row. The page does not name the sensors, reports no uncertainty or abstention, and code is only announced. Pose level, hard output, nothing on lane level or route. Verdict watch; read the full text for the sensor set and accuracy once code appears.
idea: Segments a BEV semantic map from multimodal sensor inputs and finds the vehicle pose by exhaustive matching against a map held in one representation shared by HD and SD maps, evaluated on nuScenes and Argoverse.

title: BEVMAPMATCH: Multimodal BEV Neural Map Matching for Robust Re-Localization of Autonomous Vehicles
text: Retrieve-then-refine registration of a BEV raster to a map patch with a multi-frame gain, the same step as our no-pose-given front end, with code on nuScenes (the repository uses UniTR BEV segmentation and a MatchAnything submodule, checkpoints on Google Drive). Blockers: lidar is part of the input, the basemap source is not stated, no uncertainty or abstention. Pose level, hard top-1 output. Verdict context; reuse the retrieve-then-refine pattern and the multi-frame gain.
idea: Re-localises a vehicle on a known map without a GNSS prior by fusing lidar and camera into BEV segmentation, retrieving candidate map patches by cross-attention, refining the best one by alignment, and using several frames (Recall@1m 39.8 percent).

title: Using Language and Road Manuals to Inform Map Reconstruction for Autonomous Driving
text: Shows that attribute-level SD information (road class, lane count, width) helps lane association at complex intersections; our route head reads a geometric SD raster, so extra channels for lane count and road class plus a width prior are a cheap test for lane-level assignment. Built on SMERF (trainable encoder, exact pose assumed), no route and no wrong-map test, dataset not named, no code. Verdict watch; try the attribute channels in the SD raster tokens.
idea: Adds structured OpenStreetMap road metadata, lane-width priors from road design manuals and centreline encodings to the SMERF lane-topology model and tests on two geographically diverse complex intersections.

title: NudgeVAD: Language-Nudged End-to-End Driving via FiLM Residuals
text: Shows how to feed a navigation signal into a frozen planner so that it equals the base model at initialisation, the same discipline as our frozen foundation and zero-initialised updates; with random commands the text input lowers ADE6s from 3.166 m to 2.806 m (page figures), a wrong-command robustness test. Language is the carrier, the planner is a camera VAD, and how reliable commands are produced is not stated; no code. Verdict watch; copy the identity-init conditioning for a route-flag adapter.
idea: Adjusts the trajectory of a frozen VAD planner with identity-initialised FiLM and a zero-initialised residual head driven by a categorical command channel, and compares reliable with random commands.

title: UniUncer: Unified Dynamic Static Uncertainty for End to End Driving
text: Extends UncAD (known) with agent uncertainty and a gate on temporal inputs; the page reports about 0.5 FPS cost, 7 percent lower L2 on nuScenes and 10.8 percent higher EPDMS on NAVSIM v2. A camera end-to-end planner, not reusable; no route flag and no wrong-map case. No code. Verdict context; the uncertainty-gated history is relevant to our time recursion (A5) and to passing vertex scale to the planner.
idea: Turns deterministic heads into Laplace regressors for static map vertices and dynamic agents, fuses the scale into object and map queries, and gates historical inputs by uncertainty in an end-to-end planner.

title: Unveiling the Surprising Efficacy of Navigation Understanding in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
text: Argues that end-to-end planners use global navigation too little and that a path plus turn-by-turn input improves following; this supports a route-aware planner input and a manoeuvre hint next to the route flag. The model is a VLA on image features, so only the representation idea is reusable for E117. The page does not state datasets or an SD-map link, nothing on abstention or wrong routes. Verdict context.
idea: Proposes Sequential Navigation Guidance, a global navigation representation of navigation paths plus turn-by-turn information, with a navigation VQA dataset and a VLA model that fuses local and global planning.

title: PriorDrive: Enhancing Online HD Mapping with Unified Vector Priors
text: Touches map trust from the prior side: one encoder for priors of different quality (SD, outdated HD, crowd-built), tested on nuScenes, Argoverse 2 and OpenLane-V2; it is only mentioned inside the UMPE note C02, no catalogue row. A query-based decoder on a trainable encoder (Hungarian), no route or pose estimation, and the page names no wrong-map test beyond outdated priors. Code is public (built on MapTRv2, one commit, prior maps and a checkpoint on ModelScope). Verdict context; compare its prior pre-training with our map-fault training (E87).
idea: Unified vector prior encoder with hybrid prior queries that integrates SD maps, outdated vendor HD maps and maps built from historical vehicle data into online HD mapping, with segment-level and point-level pre-training.

title: Bayesian Simultaneous Localization and Multi-Lane Tracking Using Onboard Sensors and a SD Map
text: A probabilistic ancestor of our problem: registration on an SD map and lane-level geometry estimated together, lane level, with uncertainty from the filter. It is a non-differentiable multi-object filter on one camera plus GNSS, tested on own highway data with lateral offsets; no route, no abstention. Verdict context; the idea of estimating map position and lane geometry in one state could guide the joint registration design.
idea: Jointly estimates the 6D vehicle pose, its position on the SD map and the 3D geometry of traffic lines from GNSS, visual odometry and lane-marking edge points with a Bayesian filter that tracks lines as extended objects with B-spline trajectories.

title: ArgoTweak: Towards Self-Updating HD Maps through Structured Priors
text: Real map changes as test data for the wrong or outdated map case: our map-fault training uses synthetic faults only, and Bateman et al. already showed a sim2real gap. Whether the priors are HD or SD is not stated on the page, the base data is not named, and it is an element-level HD update task, not route assignment. The paper is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Verdict watch; check whether atomic changes can be applied to an SD route for a realistic wrong-map test.
idea: First dataset pairing realistic map priors, current maps and sensor data, with a bijective framework that splits large map modifications into atomic per-element changes, to cut the sim2real gap of synthetic priors.

title: Driver2Map: Imitating Human Driving for Online High-Definition Map Construction
text: Its two-stage alignment (coarse during data preparation, fine inside the model) is a published treatment of SD-map misalignment, the registration part of our task, but only described at abstract level and it uses camera pose as input. Trainable BEV encoder with a vector decoder, dataset not named on the page, no route, no abstention, no code. Verdict context; read the full text for the fine-alignment module before designing our registration head.
idea: Online HD map model fusing multi-view images, SD maps and satellite images with a two-stage alignment strategy, pose-guided BEV fusion and a pretrained prior module for map refinement.

title: LDMapNet-U: An End-to-End System for City-Scale Lane-Level Map Updating
text: A production example of learned association between a new perception and a prior map with change prediction, which is the map-discrepancy half of map trust. Sensors and the HD or SD nature of the prior are not stated on the page, hard or soft association is not stated, no code. Verdict context; check the full text for the instance change head as a template for a per-vertex map-agrees output.
idea: End-to-end lane-level map updating that encodes the historical map as a reference and predicts associations with it, giving vectorised map elements and change information together; deployed at Baidu Maps since April 2024.

title: Learning-Based Hierarchical Scene Graph Matching for Robot Localization Leveraging Prior Maps
text: Not a driving paper (indoor, lidar), but it matches a perceived graph to a prior graph coarse to fine, which parallels road level first and lane level second, and it is trained on synthetic prior graphs only, as our simulated SD map is. It is differentiable; unmatched and outlier handling is not stated on the page; no code. Verdict context; the idea of typed edges across hierarchy levels for road-to-lane assignment.
idea: A learned, end-to-end differentiable hierarchical scene-graph matcher with semantic edge types within and between hierarchy levels, matching from rooms down to wall surfaces, trained only on floor plans and evaluated on real lidar environments.

title: Mosaic: An Extensible Framework for Composing Rule-Based and Learned Motion Planners
text: A nuPlan test bed in which a rule-based centre-line planner and a learned planner sit behind one verifier, usable to compare ground-truth, perceived and degraded lane graphs in a closed loop, the missing planner-aware metric of OVERVIEW section 3. The repository composes PDM-Closed with FlowDrive plus an emergency stop, and neither the abstract nor the README describes route or lane-graph handling; it is evaluation tooling, not a differentiable consumer. Verdict context; check the PDM wiring for a route-graph hook.
idea: Combines rule-based and learned planners through arbitration graphs with centralised trajectory verification and per-step selection; reports 95.56 CLS-NR and 94.18 CLS-R on nuPlan Val14 and 54.10 CLS-R on interPlan.

title: PriorEye: Geospatial Visual Priors for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
text: The gate with a fallback memory when retrieved priors are unreliable is the same pattern as a map-trust switch with a road-level fallback. The prior itself is route-anchored street-view imagery, which we do not have, and the page says nothing on lane level or SD maps; plug-in for camera planners. No code, project page only. Verdict context; compare the compatibility gate with our abstention design.
idea: Adds street-level visual priors anchored to the intended route to end-to-end planners through a contextual memory, a persistent fallback memory and an adaptive gate that weights each by its compatibility with the current state, evaluated on NAVSIM-v2.

title: Enhancing Online Road Network Perception and Reasoning with Standard Definition Maps
text: IROS 2024 study of SD priors in BEV architectures: SD encoders adapt quickly, and graph-form SD input is lighter than raster, a hint for our SD tokens in the route head (E104b). It is named inside note PL44 without a catalogue row. Camera input, no route, no pose noise or wrong-map test on the page, project page only. Verdict context; overlaps SMERF, P-MapNet and SMART, already known.
idea: Tests rasterised SD map inputs and SD map graphs in several online mapping architectures on OpenLane-V2 extended with OpenStreetMap, reporting faster convergence, 30 percent higher centreline mAP and fewer parameters.

title: BLOS-BEV: Navigation Map Enhanced Lane Segmentation Network Beyond Line of Sight
text: Shows the SD map as a beyond-line-of-sight prior: far-range lane structure comes mostly from the map, which suits our 100 m raster limit and the ADASIS-like horizon. Segmentation raster, not a graph; trainable camera encoder, route not used, pose assumed, no code. Verdict context; relevant only if the horizon is extended beyond the 50 m BEV.
